items.text: The delay ___ be caused by the new firewall, but we have not checked the logs yet.

ok.de: Vorsichtige Möglichkeit: might/could/may + Grundform statt einer festen Behauptung.
ok.en: Cautious possibility: might/could/may + base form instead of a flat claim.

wrong.de: must drückt Sicherheit aus, ihr habt aber noch nicht geprüft.
wrong.en: must expresses certainty, but you have not checked yet.

wrong.de: shall passt nicht zu einer vermuteten Ursache.
wrong.en: shall does not fit a suspected cause.

wrong.de: would braucht eine Bedingung (if …); hier steht keine.
wrong.en: would needs a condition (if …); there is none here.

items.text: The new vendor ___ be cheaper than our current one, but we need to compare both offers first.

ok.de: Noch nicht belegt, also vorsichtig: might/may/could be statt is.
ok.en: Not yet proven, so cautious: might/may/could be instead of is.

wrong.de: must wäre eine Schlussfolgerung mit Sicherheit; der Vergleich steht noch aus.
wrong.en: must would be a confident conclusion; the comparison is still to come.

wrong.de: shall passt nicht zu einer Vermutung über Preise.
wrong.en: shall does not fit a guess about prices.

wrong.de: would ohne if-Satz klingt unvollständig.
wrong.en: would without an if-clause sounds incomplete.

items.text: It might ___ worth checking the contract once more before we sign anything on Friday.

ok.de: Höfliche Empfehlung: It might be worth + -ing.
ok.en: A polite suggestion: It might be worth + -ing.

wrong.de: Nach might steht die Grundform be, nicht is.
wrong.en: After might comes the base form be, not is.

wrong.de: might been ist keine Form; es braucht be oder have been.
wrong.en: might been is not a form; it needs be or have been.

wrong.de: might being gibt es nicht; nach einem Modalverb steht die Grundform.
wrong.en: might being does not exist; a modal verb takes the base form.

items.text: Personally, I would be inclined ___ wait for the second quote before we make a final decision.

ok.de: Eigene Neigung vorsichtig sagen: I would be inclined to + Grundform.
ok.en: Stating your own leaning cautiously: I would be inclined to + base form.

wrong.de: inclined for + Grundform gibt es nicht; es heißt inclined to + Grundform.
wrong.en: inclined for + base form does not exist; it is inclined to + base form.

wrong.de: inclined of ist keine Wendung.
wrong.en: inclined of is not a phrase.

wrong.de: inclined at ist keine Wendung.
wrong.en: inclined at is not a phrase.

items.text: It seems as ___ the client has changed his mind about the budget, because nobody has replied to our offer.

ok.de: Eindruck vorsichtig ausdrücken: It seems as if/as though + Satz.
ok.en: Expressing an impression cautiously: It seems as if/as though + clause.

wrong.de: as when ist keine Wendung nach seems; es heißt as if oder as though.
wrong.en: as when is not used after seems; it is as if or as though.

wrong.de: unless heißt „außer wenn“ und passt nicht nach as.
wrong.en: unless means “except if” and does not follow as.

wrong.de: as since gibt es nicht.
wrong.en: as since does not exist.

items.text: To be honest, the new interface is ___ quite as intuitive as the old one, at least for our sales team.

ok.de: Weiche Kritik: not quite + as … as, ohne „schlechter“ zu sagen.
ok.en: Soft criticism: not quite + as … as, without saying “worse”.

wrong.de: very quite gibt es nicht; very und quite stehen nicht zusammen.
wrong.en: very quite does not exist; very and quite do not go together.

wrong.de: too quite gibt es nicht.
wrong.en: too quite does not exist.

wrong.de: so quite gibt es nicht; „not quite as … as“ ist die weiche Kritik.
wrong.en: so quite does not exist; “not quite as … as” is the soft criticism.

items.text: This time next week, we will ___ sitting on a beach in Portugal, far away from our inboxes.

ok.de: Was zu einem künftigen Zeitpunkt gerade läuft: will be + -ing.
ok.en: What will be in progress at a future moment: will be + -ing.

wrong.de: will are gibt es nicht; nach will steht die Grundform be.
wrong.en: will are does not exist; will takes the base form be.

wrong.de: will been ist falsch; will be + -ing ist die Form.
wrong.en: will been is wrong; will be + -ing is the form.

wrong.de: will being ist falsch; nach will steht be.
wrong.en: will being is wrong; will is followed by be.

items.text: At ___ time tomorrow, I will be meeting the new CFO in Zurich, so I will not read any e-mails.

ok.de: This time tomorrow nennt den künftigen Zeitpunkt, an dem die Handlung läuft: will be meeting.
ok.en: This time tomorrow names the future moment when the action is in progress: will be meeting.

wrong.de: at the time tomorrow passt nicht; es braucht this time.
wrong.en: at the time tomorrow does not fit; it needs this time.

wrong.de: at any time tomorrow heißt „jederzeit“, nicht „zu dieser Uhrzeit“.
wrong.en: at any time tomorrow means “whenever”, not “at this hour”.

wrong.de: at each time tomorrow ist keine Wendung.
wrong.en: at each time tomorrow is not a phrase.

items.text: ___ you be using the projector at two, or can I borrow it for a short customer call?

ok.de: Höfliche Frage nach Plänen: Will you be + -ing? klingt weniger drängend als Are you going to …?
ok.en: A polite question about plans: Will you be + -ing? sounds less pushy than Are you going to …?

wrong.de: Are you be using ist falsch; mit be + -ing braucht es Will you be using.
wrong.en: Are you be using is wrong; with be + -ing it is Will you be using.

wrong.de: Do you be using gibt es nicht.
wrong.en: Do you be using does not exist.

wrong.de: Can you be using ist keine Form.
wrong.en: Can you be using is not a form.

items.text: By the end of this quarter, we will ___ signed fifty new customers in the Nordic region.

ok.de: Bis zu einem künftigen Zeitpunkt abgeschlossen: will have + Partizip.
ok.en: Completed by a future moment: will have + participle.

wrong.de: will be signed wäre Passiv; hier sind wir die, die unterschreiben lassen: will have signed.
wrong.en: will be signed would be passive; here we are the ones doing it: will have signed.

wrong.de: will had gibt es nicht; nach will steht have.
wrong.en: will had does not exist; will is followed by have.

wrong.de: will has gibt es nicht; nach will steht immer have.
wrong.en: will has does not exist; will is always followed by have.

items.text: By the time you read this message, I will already ___ boarded the plane to Singapore.

ok.de: By the time + Gegenwart, im Hauptsatz will have + Partizip: schon passiert bis dahin.
ok.en: By the time + present, the main clause takes will have + participle: already done by then.

wrong.de: will be boarded wäre Passiv; gemeint ist die Handlung des Sprechers.
wrong.en: will be boarded would be passive; the speaker's own action is meant.

wrong.de: will had gibt es nicht; nach will steht have.
wrong.en: will had does not exist; will is followed by have.

wrong.de: will has gibt es nicht; nach will steht have.
wrong.en: will has does not exist; will is followed by have.

items.text: Next June, I will have ___ working for this company for exactly ten years.

ok.de: Dauer bis zu einem künftigen Zeitpunkt: will have been + -ing.
ok.en: Duration up to a future moment: will have been + -ing.

wrong.de: will have be ist falsch; die Form heißt will have been + -ing.
wrong.en: will have be is wrong; the form is will have been + -ing.

wrong.de: will have being ist falsch.
wrong.en: will have being is wrong.

wrong.de: will have was gibt es nicht.
wrong.en: will have was does not exist.

items.text: By December, she will have been managing the sales team ___ nearly eight years.

ok.de: Länge der Zeit mit for: will have been managing for nearly eight years.
ok.en: A length of time takes for: will have been managing for nearly eight years.

wrong.de: since braucht einen Zeitpunkt („since 2017“), hier steht eine Länge.
wrong.en: since needs a point in time (“since 2017”), but here is a length.

wrong.de: in nearly eight years passt nicht zu will have been managing.
wrong.en: in nearly eight years does not fit will have been managing.

wrong.de: during nennt keinen Gesamtzeitraum bis zu einem Zeitpunkt.
wrong.en: during does not name a total span up to a point.

items.text: By the time the CEO arrived at the venue, the presentation ___ already started without her.

ok.de: Das frühere von zwei Ereignissen in der Vergangenheit: had + Partizip.
ok.en: The earlier of two past events: had + participle.

wrong.de: has already started gehört zur Gegenwart; hier geht es um früher als „arrived“.
wrong.en: has already started is present; here the action is earlier than “arrived”.

wrong.de: have passt nicht zu presentation (Singular) und nicht zur Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: have does not fit presentation (singular) or the past.

wrong.de: is already started ist keine Zeitform.
wrong.en: is already started is not a tense.

items.text: I could not open the door of my flat because I ___ left my keys at the office again.

ok.de: Was vor „could not“ passiert war: had left (Past Perfect).
ok.en: What had happened before “could not”: had left (past perfect).

wrong.de: have left passt zur Gegenwart; „could not“ liegt schon in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: have left is present; “could not” is already in the past.

wrong.de: was left wäre Passiv; gemeint ist, dass ich sie liegen ließ.
wrong.en: was left would be passive; what is meant is that I left them.

wrong.de: did left gibt es nicht; nach did steht die Grundform.
wrong.en: did left does not exist; did takes the base form.

items.text: We had ___ waiting for the client for two hours when he finally called to cancel the meeting.

ok.de: Dauer vor einem Zeitpunkt in der Vergangenheit: had been + -ing.
ok.en: Duration before a past point: had been + -ing.

wrong.de: had be waiting ist falsch; die Form heißt had been + -ing.
wrong.en: had be waiting is wrong; the form is had been + -ing.

wrong.de: had being waiting ist falsch.
wrong.en: had being waiting is wrong.

wrong.de: had was waiting gibt es nicht.
wrong.en: had was waiting does not exist.

items.text: She looked exhausted because she had been working ___ six o'clock that morning without a single break.

ok.de: Startpunkt der Dauer: since six o'clock (oder from six o'clock).
ok.en: The starting point of the duration: since six o'clock (or from six o'clock).

wrong.de: for braucht eine Länge („for ten hours“), hier steht eine Uhrzeit.
wrong.en: for needs a length of time (“for ten hours”), but here is a clock time.

wrong.de: during passt nicht vor einer Uhrzeit.
wrong.en: during does not fit before a clock time.

wrong.de: by heißt „spätestens um“; hier ist der Anfang gemeint.
wrong.en: by means “no later than”; the start is meant here.

items.text: It was the first time I ___ ever spoken to a customer in Japanese, and I was very nervous.

ok.de: It was the first time + had + Partizip: die Erfahrung liegt vor „was“.
ok.en: It was the first time + had + participle: the experience lies before “was”.

wrong.de: have passt zur Gegenwart; „It was“ steht schon in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: have is present; “It was” is already in the past.

wrong.de: did spoken gibt es nicht; nach did steht die Grundform.
wrong.en: did spoken does not exist; did takes the base form.

wrong.de: was spoken wäre Passiv: „mit mir wurde gesprochen“.
wrong.en: was spoken would be passive: “was spoken to”.

items.text: It was the first time he had ___ been to a trade fair, so everything felt new and exciting.

ok.de: the first time + had ever + Partizip: in meinem Leben bis dahin.
ok.en: the first time + had ever + participle: in his life up to then.

wrong.de: never plus „first time“ ergibt eine doppelte Verneinung.
wrong.en: never plus “first time” makes a double negative.

wrong.de: yet passt nicht zwischen had und been in dieser Aussage.
wrong.en: yet does not fit between had and been in this statement.

wrong.de: already bedeutet „schon“ und widerspricht „first time“.
wrong.en: already means “by then” and contradicts “first time”.

items.text: She told me that the board ___ already approved the budget the day before the announcement.

ok.de: Berichtete Rede in der Vergangenheit: have/has + Partizip wird zu had + Partizip.
ok.en: Reported speech in the past: have/has + participle becomes had + participle.

wrong.de: has gehört zur Gegenwart; nach „told“ rutscht have/has einen Schritt zurück zu had.
wrong.en: has is present; after “told” have/has moves one step back to had.

wrong.de: have wird in der berichteten Rede zu had.
wrong.en: have becomes had in reported speech.

wrong.de: would approved gibt es nicht; had + Partizip steht für das Frühere.
wrong.en: would approved does not exist; had + participle expresses the earlier action.

items.text: He said that he ___ call me the next day, but I never heard from him again.

ok.de: Berichtete Rede in der Vergangenheit: will wird zu would, tomorrow zu the next day.
ok.en: Reported speech in the past: will becomes would, tomorrow becomes the next day.

wrong.de: will wird nach „said“ in der Vergangenheit zu would.
wrong.en: will becomes would after “said” in the past.

wrong.de: had call gibt es nicht; had braucht ein Partizip (called).
wrong.en: had call does not exist; had needs a participle (called).

wrong.de: has call gibt es nicht.
wrong.en: has call does not exist.

items.text: No sooner had we signed the contract ___ the client asked for several changes to the terms.

ok.de: No sooner had + Subjekt + Partizip … than: kaum war etwas passiert, passierte das Nächste.
ok.en: No sooner had + subject + participle … than: hardly had one thing happened when the next did.

wrong.de: when gehört zu Hardly … when; zu No sooner gehört than.
wrong.en: when belongs to Hardly … when; No sooner takes than.

wrong.de: then ist kein Bindewort für diesen Vergleich.
wrong.en: then is not the linking word for this comparison.

wrong.de: that passt nicht nach No sooner had …
wrong.en: that does not fit after No sooner had …

items.text: Hardly had we arrived at the hotel ___ it started to rain heavily, so we stayed in for the evening.

ok.de: Hardly had + Subjekt + Partizip … when: kaum angekommen, schon passierte das Nächste.
ok.en: Hardly had + subject + participle … when: hardly arrived, the next thing happened.

wrong.de: than gehört zu No sooner; nach Hardly steht traditionell when.
wrong.en: than belongs to No sooner; after Hardly the standard word is when.

wrong.de: then ist kein Bindewort für diesen Satz.
wrong.en: then is not the linking word for this sentence.

wrong.de: while heißt „während“ und beschreibt Gleichzeitigkeit, hier folgt aber eins auf das andere.
wrong.en: while means “during” and describes simultaneity, but here one thing follows the other.

items.text: We ___ to work in a small office near the station before the company grew to two hundred people.

ok.de: Frühere Gewohnheit oder Lage, die es nicht mehr gibt: used to + Grundform.
ok.en: A past habit or situation that no longer exists: used to + base form.

wrong.de: use to ohne did ist falsch; in der Aussage heißt es used to.
wrong.en: use to without did is wrong; in a statement it is used to.

wrong.de: would to work gibt es nicht; would steht ohne to.
wrong.en: would to work does not exist; would takes no to.

wrong.de: did to work gibt es nicht; did steht mit use to in Fragen und Verneinungen.
wrong.en: did to work does not exist; did goes with use to in questions and negatives.

items.text: Every Friday afternoon, our old boss ___ invite the whole team for coffee and talk about the week.

ok.de: Wiederholte Handlungen in der Vergangenheit: would + Grundform („every Friday“).
ok.en: Repeated actions in the past: would + base form (“every Friday”).

wrong.de: used invite gibt es nicht; es heißt used to invite.
wrong.en: used invite does not exist; it is used to invite.

wrong.de: did invite wäre betont und einmalig, nicht „jeden Freitag“.
wrong.en: did invite would be emphatic and one-off, not “every Friday”.

wrong.de: was invite gibt es nicht.
wrong.en: was invite does not exist.

items.text: Did you ___ to work from home before the pandemic, or was it always an office job?

ok.de: Fragen und Verneinungen: did + use to (ohne d).
ok.en: Questions and negatives: did + use to (without d).

wrong.de: Nach did steht use, nicht used: Did you use to …
wrong.en: After did comes use, not used: Did you use to …

wrong.de: use to hat kein -ing; nach did steht die Grundform.
wrong.en: use to has no -ing; after did the base form is used.

wrong.de: Did you would gibt es nicht.
wrong.en: Did you would does not exist.

items.text: I did not ___ to like jazz, but now I listen to it almost every evening after work.

ok.de: Verneinung früherer Gewohnheiten: did not + use to.
ok.en: Negating past habits: did not + use to.

wrong.de: Nach did not steht use, nicht used.
wrong.en: After did not comes use, not used.

wrong.de: use to hat kein -ing.
wrong.en: use to has no -ing form.

wrong.de: did not get to like wäre eine andere Wendung („dazu kommen, etwas zu mögen“).
wrong.en: did not get to like would be a different phrase (“to come to like”).

items.text: After ten years in Spain, she is completely ___ to eating dinner at ten o'clock at night.

ok.de: Schon gewöhnt: be used to + -ing oder Nomen.
ok.en: Already accustomed: be used to + -ing or noun.

wrong.de: is use to gibt es nicht; die Wendung heißt be used to.
wrong.en: is use to does not exist; the phrase is be used to.

wrong.de: is got to ist keine Form; gewöhnt sein heißt is used to.
wrong.en: is got to is not a form; being accustomed is is used to.

wrong.de: is getting to eating wäre „kommen dazu“, nicht „gewöhnt sein“.
wrong.en: is getting to eating would be “come to”, not “be accustomed”.

items.text: It took me a few weeks to get used ___ the new software, but now I could not work without it.

ok.de: Sich gewöhnen: get used to + Nomen oder -ing.
ok.en: Becoming accustomed: get used to + noun or -ing.

wrong.de: get used for hat eine andere Bedeutung („verwendet werden für“).
wrong.en: get used for has a different meaning (“be used for”).

wrong.de: get used with ist falsch; es heißt get used to.
wrong.en: get used with is wrong; it is get used to.

wrong.de: get used at ist keine Wendung.
wrong.en: get used at is not a phrase.

items.text: I am not ___ to working without a second monitor, so the trip to the client site is a challenge.

ok.de: Nicht gewöhnt an etwas: not be used to + -ing.
ok.en: Not accustomed to something: not be used to + -ing.

wrong.de: am not use to gibt es nicht; die Wendung heißt be used to.
wrong.en: am not use to does not exist; the phrase is be used to.

wrong.de: am not getting to working ist keine Wendung.
wrong.en: am not getting to working is not a phrase.

wrong.de: am not going to working wäre „ich gehe nicht zur Arbeit“.
wrong.en: am not going to working would mean “I am not going to work”.

items.text: I was wondering ___ you could send me the updated price list by tomorrow afternoon.

ok.de: Weiche Bitte: I was wondering if/whether you could … (Vergangenheitsform macht es höflicher).
ok.en: A soft request: I was wondering if/whether you could … (the past form makes it more polite).

wrong.de: wondering that passt nicht vor einer Bitte; gebraucht wird if oder whether.
wrong.en: wondering that does not fit before a request; if or whether is needed.

wrong.de: wondering when fragt nach einem Zeitpunkt, nicht nach einer Bitte.
wrong.en: wondering when asks for a point in time, not a request.

wrong.de: unless heißt „außer wenn“ und leitet keine höfliche Frage ein.
wrong.en: unless means “except if” and does not introduce a polite question.

items.text: We were hoping ___ extend the deadline by two days, if that would be possible for your team.

ok.de: Höflicher Wunsch: We were hoping to + Grundform.
ok.en: A polite wish: We were hoping to + base form.

wrong.de: hoping for braucht ein Nomen, hier folgt ein Verb.
wrong.en: hoping for needs a noun, but a verb follows here.

wrong.de: hoping that braucht einen ganzen Satz mit Subjekt.
wrong.en: hoping that needs a full clause with a subject.

wrong.de: hoping of gibt es nicht.
wrong.en: hoping of does not exist.

items.text: Would it be possible ___ move the meeting to Thursday morning, because several people are travelling on Wednesday?

ok.de: Höfliche Frage: Would it be possible + to + Grundform?
ok.en: A polite question: Would it be possible + to + base form?

wrong.de: possible for braucht eine Person danach („for us to move“).
wrong.en: possible for needs a person after it (“for us to move”).

wrong.de: possible if + Grundform passt nicht; if braucht einen ganzen Satz.
wrong.en: possible if + base form does not fit; if needs a full clause.

wrong.de: possible that braucht einen Satz mit Subjekt.
wrong.en: possible that needs a clause with a subject.

items.text: Would it be possible ___ us to join the call about ten minutes late, because of a customer meeting?

ok.de: Mit Person: Would it be possible for us to + Grundform?
ok.en: With a person: Would it be possible for us to + base form?

wrong.de: possible to us ist falsch; vor der Person steht for.
wrong.en: possible to us is wrong; for goes before the person.

wrong.de: possible if us ist falsch.
wrong.en: possible if us is wrong.

wrong.de: possible that us ist falsch.
wrong.en: possible that us is wrong.

items.text: Honestly, that deadline could be a bit of ___ stretch for our team, given the holidays in December.

ok.de: Weiche Kritik: could be a bit of a stretch klingt freundlicher als „is impossible“.
ok.en: Soft objection: could be a bit of a stretch sounds friendlier than “is impossible”.

wrong.de: a bit of the stretch ist keine feste Wendung; es heißt a bit of a stretch.
wrong.en: a bit of the stretch is not the fixed phrase; it is a bit of a stretch.

wrong.de: an steht vor Vokalen; stretch beginnt mit s.
wrong.en: an goes before vowel sounds; stretch begins with s.

wrong.de: a bit of one stretch gibt es nicht.
wrong.en: a bit of one stretch does not exist.
